stem: Five people sit in a row of five seats numbered 1 (leftmost) to 5 (rightmost): Ajay, Birju, Chhaya, Dhruv, and Esha. The following clues apply: (1) Esha sits at the rightmost seat. (2) Birju, Chhaya, and Dhruv occupy three consecutive seats in that left-to-right order. (3) Ajay does not sit in any of the last three seats (seats 3, 4, or 5). Who sits in the fourth seat from the left?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Esha=5, Ajay=1 (only end not taken by Esha and satisfying clue 3), leaving seats 2-3-4 for Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv in order; seat 4 = Dhruv.
Student ignores clue 3, places Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv at seats 1-2-3, and puts Ajay at seat 4.
Student reverses clue 1, treating Esha as the leftmost (seat 1) instead of rightmost; this forces Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv to seats 3-4-5, putting Ajay at seat 2 and Chhaya at seat 4.
Student reads clue 2 right-to-left (turning the stated left-to-right order around), placing Dhruv-Chhaya-Birju at seats 2-3-4, giving seat 4 = Birju.

explanation: Clue 1 fixes Esha at seat 5. Clue 3 limits Ajay to seat 1 or 2; since Esha holds seat 5 and the Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv block (clue 2) needs three consecutive seats, testing the block at seats 1-2-3 forces Ajay to seat 4 or 5 (violates clue 3), so the block sits at seats 2-3-4 with Ajay at seat 1. Seat 4 = Dhruv.

explanation_sections.punchline: Lock Esha at seat 5 first (clue 1). Clue 3 forces Ajay to seat 1 or 2. The only block position that keeps seats 1 or 2 for Ajay is seats 2-3-4 for Birju-Chhaya-Dhruv. Seat 4 = Dhruv.
explanation_sections.approach: Work clues in order of certainty: fixed-seat clues first, then ordered-block clues, then negative clues. Step 1: Clue 1 places Esha at seat 5. Step 2: Clue 3 restricts Ajay to seats 1 or 2 (not 3, 4, 5). Step 3: Clue 2 requires a consecutive block B-C-D, which can start at seat 1 (occupying 1-2-3) or seat 2 (occupying 2-3-4). Test seat 1: block at 1-2-3 leaves Ajay at seat 4 or 5 only, violating clue 3. Eliminated. Test seat 2: block at 2-3-4 leaves Ajay at seat 1, satisfying clue 3. Confirmed. Seat 4 = Dhruv (third in block). Verify all three clues against the final row.
explanation_sections.lesson: When a block and a boundary clue compete for the same seats, test each starting position for the block and reject any that push the constrained person into a banned seat. One test usually eliminates all but one option.
explanation_sections.timing: About 75 seconds. Placing Esha takes 5 seconds. Two block-position tests take 15 seconds each. The clue-3 violation at position 1-2-3 is immediate. Option Ajay at seat 4 is the trap for students who skip clue 3.
